caseno: Criminal Appeal No. 1088 of 1990 (Dhaka) Criminal Appeal No. 52 of 1989 (Comilla)
lawyer:
Serajul Hoque with ABM Golam Majid, Nurul Islam Sujan and Anisur Rahman, Advocates — For the Appellant
Md. Abdus Salam Mamun, Assistant Attorney-General — For the State
full_judgment: 11. It is in evidence of PW 1 that a Hindu family having 6 members resides in the northern part of their house but PW 12 denied the suggestion that they came at the time of occurrence. Since there is no evidence that any member of that family came there and that they being members of the minority community it is not unnatural for them to keep themselves aloof from the said occurrence. There is also no evidence that any other persons than the PWs came to the place of occurrence house immediately after the occurrence and prosecution was withholding them. In such circumstances no adverse presumption could be made against the prosecution for not examining such unnamed witnesses. As to the grievance of examination of the PWs long after the occurrence it is in evidence of first Investigation Officer PW 16 that he examined and recorded statements of some of the witnesses and made over case diary to SI Nazrul Islam after his transfer on 14.7.88 whereas PW 17 stated that he examined some of the witnesses after taking over the investigation on 1.8.88 and after consulting the papers and evidence submitted charge-sheet on 15.10.88 against the accused appellant. Learned Assistant Attorney-General pointing out to the same submitted that the PW 17 might have examined some of the witnesses but did not record their statements which was already recorded by PW 16. PW 5 stated that he was examined by Investigation Officer on 20.4.88. and not on 8.10.88 PW 6 stated that he was examined on 20.4.88 and not on 3.10.88. PW 12 stated that she was examined on 20.4.88 and not after 4 months. PW 16 denied the suggestion that he did not examine PWs 5 6 and 12 on 20.4.88 whereas PW 17 said that he examined PW 12 on 7.8.88 PW 5 on 8.10.88 and PW 6 on 3.10.88 but did not say that he recorded their statements on those dates and their statements were not recorded by PW 6. In such circumstances we find substance in the submissions of the learned Assistant Attorney -General and no substance in the submission of the learned Advocate of the appellant in this respect. So decision in the case of State vs. Paran Bari reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 223 has no manner of application in the present appeal before us.
